title: 'I did expect him to kill her sometime': Relative of woman shot in hospital says husband bragged about gun
subtitle: Ontario Provincial Police are investigating the death of Helen Ryan and the Special Investigations Unit is investigating the death of Tom Ryan
article: A relative of the woman shot dead at Northumberland Hills Hospital Friday believes the woman's husband killed her before he was killed by police.
On Friday evening at about 11 p.m. a woman was shot in the head in the emergency area of the hospital.
Police responded immediately.
Connie Woodcock said her cousin, Helen Ryan, was shot by her husband, Tom (William) before he was shot by police.
Both died on scene from their injuries.
OPP are investigating the death of Helen Ryan and the Special Investigations Unit is investigating the death of Tom Ryan.
Woodcock said she almost expected something like this to happen.
"I did expect him to kill her sometime. We are all shocked it happened, but not terribly surprised," she said. "He was a violent, horrible man."
Woodcock said Ryan was controlling.

"He had threatened Helen many times. She had no money of her own," she said. "I thought at times that she was right over the edge too, except when I spent time with her she started to be more normal and like the person I knew as a kid. He completely had her under his thumb."
The Ryans visited cousins in Brighton about three years ago and he showed off a firearm, "bragging about bringing it across the border," Woodcock said.
He once stated he had more than 700 firearms.
Helen grew up in Campbellford while Tom grew up in Toronto.
"Helen was a dear, sweet woman, who had an operatic soprano voice and sang beautifully when she was younger," Woodcock said.
"I often wondered if there was any way to get her away from him."
He worked for a major oil manufacturer, setting up computers for the company around the world and becoming very wealthy. With that wealth he started to collect guns.
"We heard from a relative he built a bunker in the basement to store the guns (in Texas)."
He'd even won an award with the National Rifle Association and had a full range in Texas.
The two were married in 1971 and though they lived just outside Houston in Texas, they spent their summers in the Northumberland area to enjoy the benefits of OHIP, said Woodcock.
On Friday, an ambulance reportedly transported Ryan to hospital from their trailer at Salem Woods Trailer Park just east of Colborne for an unknown medical condition.
It's believed his wife was in the ambulance with him at the time.

The couple had been living in the trailer at Castleton Hills RV Park, but when it closed for the season they moved the trailer to a spot east of Colborne. They reportedly planned to return to Texas later this month.

Though she can't imagine what transpired at the hospital on Friday evening, "I wanted to the true story to come out. Because I feel guilty because I knew about that gun," Woodcock said. "How the hell did he get that gun in there? It's tragic."
